description.value: The study compares the diagnostic utility of ASL-MRI cerebral blood flow and FDG-PET cerebral metabolic rate of glucose maps for differentiating behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia, Alzheimer's disease, and cognitively normal controls.

spans.text: To compare the values of arterial spin‐labeled (ASL) MRI and fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET in the diagnosis of behavioral variant of frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) and Alzheimer's disease (AD).

description.value: The study included 32 patients with bvFTD, 28 patients with AD, and 15 clinically normal (CN) elderly individuals. Both neuroimaging evaluations occurred within a 180-day period.

name.value: AD versus CN classification using CBF-based scores

spans.text: In AD versus CN classification, areas under the curve for CMRgl‐based (0.91, 95% CI: 0.77–1.00) and CBF‐based scores (0.89, 95% CI: 0.76–1.00) were similar with similar sensitivity (CMRgl‐based 78%, CBF‐based 86%) and specificity (CMRgl‐based 100%, CBF‐based 92%).
For differentiating AD from CN, the areas under the curve (AUC) for CBF (0.89) and CMRgl (0.91) were similar, with similar sensitivity (CBF: 86%, CMRgl: 78%) and specificity (CBF: 92%, CMRgl: 100%).
